questions.stem: A leaf in full sun loses most of its heat by evaporating water from the moist surfaces inside it. Which property of water most directly makes that cooling effective?
options: Water's high heat of vaporization, because each gram that evaporates carries away a large amount of absorbed energy
Water's high specific heat, because it absorbs energy before its own temperature rises
Water's cohesion, because molecules pull one another through the xylem
Water's polarity, because dissolved ions carry heat out of the leaf
questions.why: Evaporation breaks the hydrogen bonds holding water in liquid form, and that takes about 2,260 joules per gram, so the leaf surface loses heat as molecules leave.

questions.stem: "The board calls this a budget cut. The teachers call it a budget choice. The students call it a lost semester." The progression mainly works to
options: establish the writer's neutrality by giving three perspectives equal weight
concede that the board's original framing was accurate
replace argument with an emotional appeal that carries no evidence
escalate from administrative language to human consequence, aligning the reader with the final term
questions.why: The three labels move from technical euphemism to personal cost, so the last term reframes the issue on the ground least favorable to the board.

questions.stem: A purified enzyme loses all catalytic activity after being held at 80 C for ten minutes, but regains most of that activity when cooled slowly. Which best explains this result?
options: The peptide bonds were hydrolyzed and then re-formed during cooling
The primary sequence was altered at high temperature and restored on cooling
Tertiary structure unfolded without breaking peptide bonds, and slow cooling let the chain refold into a functional active site
The enzyme was phosphorylated at high temperature and later dephosphorylated
questions.why: Heat disrupts the weak interactions holding tertiary shape. The primary sequence is untouched, so removing the heat lets the chain fold back into its native conformation.

questions.stem: A district's later start time raised attendance but also raised busing costs. Which sentence works best as a thesis for an essay weighing that trade-off?
options: Later start times are the single most effective reform available to American high schools.
Later start times raise attendance enough to justify added transportation costs in most districts, though the trade-off depends on existing bus routes.
Later start times improve attendance and are therefore always worth whatever they cost.
Later start times are controversial, since some people support them and others do not.
questions.why: A defensible thesis takes a position while naming the condition under which it holds. The others either overclaim absolutely or say nothing anyone could dispute.

questions.stem: An inhibitor binds an enzyme's active site reversibly. Adding excess substrate restores the original maximum reaction rate. Which conclusion does this support?
options: The inhibitor is competitive, because substrate can displace it from the active site
The inhibitor is noncompetitive, because it changes the enzyme's maximum rate
The inhibitor permanently lowers the enzyme's affinity for its substrate
The inhibitor denatures the enzyme irreversibly at low substrate concentration
questions.why: Competitive inhibitors raise the apparent Km but leave Vmax unchanged, since enough substrate outcompetes them. A noncompetitive inhibitor would lower Vmax and could not be reversed this way.

questions.stem: A student argues that a district's new phone policy reduced hallway disruptions. Which evidence would most strengthen that claim?
options: A single teacher's account that the halls feel calmer this year
A survey showing that most students dislike the policy
Disruption referrals fell 40 percent in the semester after the policy, while nearby districts without such a policy stayed flat
The fact that the policy was announced in a widely read newsletter
questions.why: This evidence supplies both a before-and-after measure and a comparison group, which rules out changes that would have happened anyway. An anecdote or an opinion poll cannot.

questions.stem: The Na+/K+ ATPase moves three Na+ out and two K+ in for each ATP hydrolyzed. A cell treated with ouabain, which blocks the pump, will most directly show
options: a large increase in intracellular ATP with ion gradients unaffected
immediate hyperpolarization as K+ rushes out of the cell
no change at all, because diffusion alone maintains the gradients
a rise in intracellular Na+, gradual osmotic swelling, and loss of the resting potential
questions.why: The pump is electrogenic and maintains the gradients. Blocking it lets Na+ leak in and K+ leak out, depolarizing the membrane while water follows Na+ inward.

questions.stem: "I asked three seniors about the new schedule and all three hated it, so the whole school opposes the change." The reasoning fails because it
options: attacks the seniors' character instead of answering their argument
generalizes from a small, self-selected sample to an entire population
assumes as a premise exactly what it sets out to prove
presents only two alternatives when more exist
questions.why: Three volunteers cannot stand in for a school of hundreds, and students who agree to be asked are not a random draw.

questions.stem: A well-watered plant is supplied with CO2 but kept in darkness for several hours. Which consequence best explains why carbon fixation slows to a stop?
options: Without the light reactions, ATP and NADPH are not regenerated, so the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle stalls
Rubisco denatures permanently in the absence of light
CO2 can no longer diffuse into the leaf because stomata require light to open
Oxygen accumulates and competitively inhibits rubisco
questions.why: The Calvin cycle spends ATP and NADPH made by the light reactions. In darkness those pools drain within minutes and fixation has nothing to run on.

questions.stem: "The board approved the calendar, after eleven months of meetings, three failed votes, and a survey of two thousand families." Compared with stating the decision first, this arrangement mainly
options: conceals the subject of the sentence until the very end
turns the sentence into a fragment by separating the modifiers
delays the outcome until the reader has the cost of reaching it, stressing how hard the decision was
lifts the passage into a more formal and distant register
questions.why: The main clause is complete early and the trailing modifiers pile up evidence. Ending on the effort makes the process, not the vote, the point.

questions.stem: Dinitrophenol carries protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane without passing through ATP synthase. Treated cells consume oxygen rapidly but make very little ATP. Which best explains this?
options: Oxygen can no longer serve as the final electron acceptor
Glycolysis is inhibited by the accumulating protons
ATP synthase is denatured and can no longer bind ADP
The proton gradient is dissipated, so the force driving ATP synthase collapses while the electron transport chain keeps running
questions.why: Uncouplers short-circuit the gradient. Electrons still flow to oxygen, which is why O2 use rises, but the energy leaves as heat instead of being captured as ATP.

questions.stem: A district announces that its plan will "streamline staffing." A critic would most likely object that the word mainly
options: borrows the neutral language of efficiency, recasting lost jobs as optimization and hiding who bears the cost
is too technical for a general audience to understand
overstates the number of positions that will actually be eliminated
introduces a statistic without naming its source
questions.why: Streamline belongs to the vocabulary of engineering, where removing parts is improvement. Applied to people, it obscures the human consequence of the cut.

questions.stem: A child with trisomy 21 inherits two chromosome 21 copies that are identical to each other, both from the mother. Which event best explains this?
options: Nondisjunction in meiosis I of the mother, so two different homologs were inherited together
Nondisjunction in meiosis II of the mother, so two identical sister chromatids were inherited together
A reciprocal translocation in the father's sperm
Crossing over between homologs during mitosis in the early embryo
questions.why: Identical copies mean sister chromatids failed to separate, which happens in meiosis II. A meiosis I error would deliver the two different maternal homologs, not duplicates.

questions.stem: "The district has, at long last, discovered the staggering innovation of asking students what they think." The tone is best described as
options: earnest and openly admiring of the district's leadership
neutral and reportorial, offering no judgment
anxious and uncertain about what the district will do next
sardonic, inflating a modest step into a breakthrough in order to mock the delay
questions.why: "At long last" and "staggering innovation" are absurdly grand for merely consulting students, and the mismatch produces irony rather than praise.

questions.stem: A dihybrid cross between two heterozygotes for unlinked genes yields 315, 108, 101, and 32 offspring in the four phenotype classes. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The two genes are linked, since the classes are not exactly equal
One of the alleles is lethal in the homozygous state
The numbers approximate the expected 9:3:3:1 ratio, consistent with independent assortment
The traits show incomplete dominance in the heterozygotes
questions.why: Of 556 offspring, the classes fall close to 9:3:3:1. Small deviations from expectation are ordinary sampling variation, not evidence of linkage or lethality.

questions.stem: "Reading scores rose the year after the district adopted a new reading program, so the program caused the gain." The flaw is that the argument
options: treats a sequence in time as proof of causation without ruling out other changes from that year
relies on a sample that is far too small to support any inference
misrepresents the position of the program's opponents
uses a technical term it never defines for the reader
questions.why: New teachers, a revised test, or a shift in enrollment could all explain the gain. Order of events alone does not establish that one caused the other.

questions.stem: A chi-square test of a monohybrid cross produces a value well above the critical value at p = 0.05. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The hypothesized ratio is supported by the data
The test cannot evaluate genetic ratios and the cross must be repeated
The two genes involved must be linked
The deviation from the expected ratio is large enough that the null hypothesis is rejected
questions.why: Exceeding the critical value means sampling error alone is an unlikely explanation, so the expected ratio is rejected at that significance level.

questions.stem: An essay arguing for later start times opens by stating the strongest objection, bus route conflicts, and answers it before presenting supporting evidence. This order mainly
options: weakens the essay by handing the opposition free space at the start
builds credibility and clears the reader's main doubt before the affirmative case begins
changes the essay's purpose from argument to description
signals that the writer has not settled on a position
questions.why: Conceding and rebutting the strongest objection up front shows fair-mindedness and removes the obstacle that would otherwise block the rest of the argument.

questions.stem: One gene produces three different proteins in three different tissues, with no change to the DNA sequence. Which mechanism best explains this?
options: Different genes are switched on in each of the three tissues
The redundancy of the genetic code allows one mRNA to encode several proteins
Alternative splicing of the pre-mRNA includes or skips different exons in each tissue
Reverse transcription rewrites the gene in each tissue
questions.why: A single pre-mRNA can be spliced into several mature mRNAs. Which exons are retained determines the protein, so one gene yields multiple isoforms.

questions.stem: "If the district cannot answer a single parent email within a week, how will it manage a semester-long schedule change?" The question functions mainly to
options: invite the audience to supply an answer that undermines the district's competence
request specific information about the district's staffing
concede that the district is overworked and deserves patience
move the passage from argument into narration
questions.why: The question seeks no data. It compresses an argument into a frame the reader completes, so the conclusion feels self-evident rather than asserted.

questions.stem: A single base is inserted near the start of a coding sequence, and the resulting protein is short and nonfunctional. Which best explains the outcome?
options: One amino acid was substituted and the rest of the protein folded normally
Proofreading enzymes removed the inserted base before translation finished
The mRNA was never transcribed, so no protein was produced
The insertion shifted the reading frame, so all downstream codons are misread and a premature stop codon truncates the protein
questions.why: Inserting a number of bases that is not a multiple of three shifts the frame. Every later codon changes, and an early stop codon usually ends translation.

questions.stem: In a synthesis essay arguing that later start times improve attendance, which use of a source would strengthen the argument most?
options: A long personal anecdote about how hard the writer's own mornings are
A district report showing attendance gains after the change, cited with an explanation of its method and limits
A quotation from a friend who dislikes the new policy
A general assertion that studies have shown benefits, without naming one
questions.why: Synthesis rewards a relevant, attributable source whose method and limitations the writer explains. Personal material and unnamed studies cannot carry the claim.

questions.stem: One hormone molecule binding a single receptor leads to thousands of activated enzyme molecules in the cytoplasm. Which feature of signal transduction explains this?
options: Receptors are continuously recycled back to the cell surface
The hormone enters the nucleus and binds DNA directly
A phosphorylation cascade amplifies the signal at each step, so one receptor event activates many effectors
The signal spreads outward by simple diffusion from the receptor
questions.why: Each activated kinase phosphorylates many substrates, and each of those activates more. The cascade multiplies a single binding event by orders of magnitude.

questions.stem: "The proposal's cost envelope exceeds the district's capital threshold, triggering a mandatory reallocation review." For an audience of parents, this diction mainly
options: creates distance by replacing the plain fact that the plan costs more than the district can pay with process language
clarifies the budget process with useful precision
appeals to the audience's feelings about their children
supplies statistical evidence for the writer's claim
questions.why: Nominalized, technical phrasing hides a simple fact behind procedure. That can obscure accountability rather than clarify what is actually being decided.

questions.stem: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16 percent of individuals show the recessive phenotype. What fraction of the population is heterozygous?
questions.why: q squared equals 0.16, so q is 0.4 and p is 0.6. The heterozygote frequency is 2pq, or 2 times 0.6 times 0.4, which is 0.48.

questions.stem: "The district's transparency initiative is a window with the blinds drawn." The metaphor mainly works by
options: comparing two unrelated objects for decorative effect
providing a statistic about how visible the records are
using a familiar image to argue that the initiative formally exists while blocking the view it promises
softening a criticism until it reads as praise
questions.why: A window promises access; drawn blinds deny it. The figure carries the argument that the policy is present in name only.

questions.stem: Two populations of the same bird species live on opposite sides of a mountain range. Where the ranges meet they occupy the same habitat and breed in the same month, yet they never interbreed. Which isolating mechanism is operating?
options: Temporal isolation, because their breeding seasons do not overlap
Behavioral or mechanical reproductive isolation, since the birds coexist and still do not interbreed
Geographic isolation alone, with no reproductive barrier involved
Gametic incompatibility caused by different pollinators
questions.why: They are sympatric at the contact zone with matching timing, so neither geography nor season separates them. A behavioral or mechanical barrier maintains the boundary.

questions.stem: "The board's response to four hundred parent signatures was, we might say, modest." The understatement mainly
options: states plainly that the board's response was adequate
offers a neutral summary of what the board actually did
shifts the argument from rhetoric into statistics
uses deliberate restraint to imply the response was inadequate, leaving the reader to supply the criticism
questions.why: Understatement says less than the situation warrants. The gap between "modest" and four hundred signatures is where the critique lives.

questions.stem: A cladogram places whales with hippos rather than with sharks. Which evidence best supports that placement?
options: Shared derived skeletal and molecular characters inherited from a common ancestor that sharks lack
The fact that both whales and hippos spend their lives in water
The fact that whales and hippos are both very large animals
The fact that sharks appeared in the fossil record earlier than whales
questions.why: Cladograms group taxa by shared derived characters from common ancestry. Shared habitat or body size reflects convergence and says nothing about relationship.

questions.stem: "If the district adopts this schedule, no student will ever get to a job on time again." The statement's main weakness is that it
options: makes a measured claim that is too cautiously qualified
relies on a statistic it never explains or sources
overstates the consequence so extremely that readers can dismiss it, costing the argument credibility
misquotes the district's actual proposal
questions.why: Hyperbole in place of evidence invites outright rejection, even where a real scheduling concern sits underneath the exaggeration.

questions.stem: After a meal, blood glucose rises well above its set point. Which response best describes the resulting hormonal control?
options: Glucagon rises and the liver releases stored glucose into the blood
Insulin rises, promoting glucose uptake and glycogen storage, and glucose falls back toward the set point
Insulin and glucagon both rise, canceling each other out
Insulin falls and glycogen breakdown in the liver increases
questions.why: High glucose triggers insulin, which drives uptake and storage. As glucose falls, insulin secretion drops, which is negative feedback around a set point.

questions.stem: An essay opens: "This essay examines how the district's new schedule was announced, funded, and defended." The sentence states a
options: an arguable thesis that takes a clear position
a counterargument the essay will go on to answer
a call to action directed at the school board
topic or purpose rather than a thesis, since it names the subject without making a claim
questions.why: Naming what an essay will examine describes its scope. A thesis must assert something contestable that the rest of the essay then defends.

questions.stem: In an exercising muscle, temperature and CO2 rise while pH falls. Which change in hemoglobin's behavior follows, and why does it matter?
options: Its affinity for oxygen decreases, so more oxygen is released exactly where demand is highest
Its affinity for oxygen increases, so less oxygen is released into the tissue
It binds CO2 irreversibly and can no longer transport oxygen
Its total oxygen-carrying capacity doubles to meet the demand
questions.why: Heat, CO2 and low pH shift the dissociation curve right, lowering affinity. That is the Bohr effect, and it unloads more oxygen where metabolism is running hardest.
